info.title: @bumail/jmap
info.summary: The HTTP surface of the JMAP server of @bumail/jmap (RFC 8620, RFC 8621).
info.description:
The routes `jmap(options)` adds to the alxia app that mounts it: the session at `/.well-known/jmap`, and, under `basePath` (`/jmap` by default), the API, blob download and blob upload. Its `info.version` is the version of the document, not of the package. It is documentation and a contract, kept in step with the routes by a spec of the package; the server does not validate requests against it.

The API is described as RFC 8620 §3 frames it: a Request of method calls and a Response of method responses, each an Invocation `[name, arguments, callId]`. The arguments of each method are left generic on purpose: an argument named `#name` is a back-reference (RFC 8620 §3.7) resolved from an earlier response, so a call's arguments are only known once the calls before it ran, and a method's error is an `error` invocation inside a 200, not an HTTP status. RFC 8620 and RFC 8621 define each method's arguments.

The limits stated are the defaults of the `limits` option; the session announces the ones in effect. The session announces an `eventSourceUrl`, as RFC 8620 requires, which no route serves yet: push is a later release.

Every route authenticates its request first, with HTTP Basic (RFC 7617) or a Bearer token (RFC 6750), and answers 401, 403 or 503 before anything else.

servers.description: The session is at `/.well-known/jmap` of the app that mounts the server, whatever `basePath` is.

origin.description: The `origin` option: the public origin the session's URLs start with.

get.description: The Session object (RFC 8620 §2) of the authenticated account: the capabilities with the core limits, the one account `authenticate` answered, and the URLs of the API, download, upload and event source, built from the `origin` and `basePath` options. Its `state` is a hash of the rest; every API response carries it as `sessionState`.

servers.description: The API, download and upload are under the `basePath` option. With another `basePath`, set this variable: the paths stay as they are.

basePath.description: The `basePath` option: a path such as `/jmap`, with no trailing slash.

post.description:
One JMAP Request (RFC 8620 §3.3): its calls run in order, each seeing the responses before it. A request refused as a whole is a problem (RFC 8620 §3.6.1) and no call runs; a call that fails is an `error` invocation in the 200 (RFC 8620 §3.6.2), and the calls after it still run.

The body is held to `maxSizeRequest` (10 MB): a `Content-Length` past it is refused unread, a chunked body at the first chunk past it. It must be UTF-8 JSON nesting at most `maxJsonDepth` (64) levels with at most `maxJsonTokens` (100 000) tokens, then a Request. Its `Content-Type` is not read. At most `maxConcurrentRequests` (4) requests of one account run at once.

200.description: The Response (RFC 8620 §3.4): one method response per call, in order, each the method's arguments or an `error`.

400.description: The request is refused as a whole (RFC 8620 §3.6.1): not UTF-8 JSON (`notJSON`), not a Request (`notRequest`), a capability in `using` the server does not have (`unknownCapability`), or a limit broken (`limit`): `maxJsonDepth`, `maxJsonTokens`, `maxCallsInRequest`, or `maxSizeResponse` once the response grows past it, the calls after that not run.

value.detail: The request body is not JSON
The server does not support the capability "urn:ietf:params:jmap:contacts"
The request makes more than 16 method calls

413.description: The body is larger than `maxSizeRequest`: a `limit` problem naming it.

example.detail: The request is larger than 10000000 bytes

429.description: The account has `maxConcurrentRequests` requests in flight already: a `limit` problem naming it. The body is not read.

example.detail: The account has 4 requests in flight already

servers.description: The API, download and upload are under the `basePath` option. With another `basePath`, set this variable: the paths stay as they are.

basePath.description: The `basePath` option: a path such as `/jmap`, with no trailing slash.

get.description:
The session's `downloadUrl` (RFC 8620 §6.2), `{basePath}/download/{accountId}/{blobId}/{name}?accept={type}`: an upload of the account, an email's content by its `blobId`, or one part of an email by the part's `blobId`, decoded from its transfer encoding. One `Range: bytes=` range is served as a 206.

Every download is `nosniff` and sandboxed by its `Content-Security-Policy`, and is `inline` only for `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp` and `text/plain`; every other type is an `attachment`.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: The authenticated account: any other, or one that is not an Id, is a 404.

parameters.name: blobId
parameters.description: The blob: one the account does not have, or one that is not an Id, is a 404.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file name for `Content-Disposition`, any text, cut to 255 code points.

parameters.name: accept
parameters.description: The `Content-Type` to serve the blob as, a media type without parameters. Left out or not a media type, the type is the part's or the upload's, else `application/octet-stream`.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: One byte range, `bytes=start-end`, `bytes=start-` or `bytes=-suffix`. Several ranges, or a header that is not one of these, is ignored and the whole blob served; so is a suffix range of an empty blob (RFC 9110 §14.1.1).

404.description: No blob of the account has this id, the account is not the authenticated one, or an id is not an Id.

416.description: The range starts at or past the end of the blob, ends before it starts, or is an empty suffix (`bytes=-0`). It has no body and no `Content-Type`, and carries none of the blob's headers.

servers.description: The API, download and upload are under the `basePath` option. With another `basePath`, set this variable: the paths stay as they are.

basePath.description: The `basePath` option: a path such as `/jmap`, with no trailing slash.

post.description: The session's `uploadUrl` (RFC 8620 §6.1). The body is held to `maxSizeUpload` (25 MiB) as the API's is to `maxSizeRequest`, and kept in memory for `uploadTtl` (3600 s); an account holds at most `uploadQuota` (100 MiB) of uploads at once, and has at most `maxConcurrentUpload` (4) in flight. The `blobId` is the SHA-256 of the bytes, so the same bytes uploaded twice are one upload.

parameters.name: accountId
parameters.description: The authenticated account: any other, or one that is not an Id, is a 404.

requestBody.description: The bytes. Their type is the `Content-Type` without its parameters, lowercased, or `application/octet-stream` when it is not a media type.

404.description: The account is not the authenticated one, or is not an Id. The body is not read.

413.description: A `limit` problem: the body is larger than `maxSizeUpload`, or the account holds `uploadQuota` bytes of uploads already.

value.detail: The upload is larger than 26214400 bytes
The account holds 104857600 bytes of uploads already: use them or wait for them to expire

429.description: The account has `maxConcurrentUpload` uploads in flight already: a `limit` problem naming it. The body is not read.

example.detail: The account has 4 uploads in flight already

basic.description: HTTP Basic (RFC 7617): base64 of UTF-8 `user:password`, the password everything after the first `:`. Refused with a 403 on a clear request — one whose URL is not `https:`, or that the `secure` option says is not — before `authenticate` is called, unless `allowInsecureBasic` is set, for local tests only.

bearer.description: A Bearer token (RFC 6750), taken on any request: the `b64token` syntax, `[A-Za-z0-9-._~+/]+=*`.

ContentDisposition.description: `inline` or `attachment`, with `filename` in ASCII and `filename*` in UTF-8 (RFC 6266, RFC 8187).

Sandbox.description: `default-src 'none'; sandbox`: a blob never runs as a page of the server's origin.

Immutable.description: `private, immutable, max-age=31536000`: a blob id names the same bytes for good.

Unauthorized.description: No credentials the server can read — no `Authorization`, another scheme, a header past 8 KiB, Basic that is not base64 of UTF-8 `user:password` — (`Authentication required`), or `authenticate` refused them (`Authentication failed`).

WWW-Authenticate.description: Sent twice: `Basic realm="JMAP", charset="UTF-8"` and `Bearer realm="JMAP"`.

BasicOnClear.description: Basic credentials on a clear request, refused unread: `authenticate` is not called.

example.detail: Basic authentication is refused on a clear connection: use HTTPS

AuthUnavailable.description: `authenticate` threw, did not settle within `hookTimeout` (30 s), answered something other than an account id or `null`, or named an account the store does not have; or the store's `getAccount` threw. `onError` is told.

Id.description: An Id (RFC 8620 §1.2): 1 to 255 characters of the URL-safe base64 alphabet.

accounts.description: One account: the one `authenticate` answered, by its id.

username.description: The account's name in the store.

eventSourceUrl.description: `{origin}{basePath}/eventsource?types={types}&closeafter={closeafter}&ping={ping}`: required by RFC 8620, and not served until push lands.

state.description: A hash of the rest of the session: it changes only when the limits, the URLs or the account's name do.

Request.description: A Request (RFC 8620 §3.3). A request that is not one is a `notRequest` problem; one past `maxCallsInRequest` (16) calls a `limit` problem.

using.description: The capabilities the calls use. A name the server does not have is an `unknownCapability` problem.

createdIds.description: Creation ids to ids, from an earlier request: at most `maxObjectsInSet` (500).

Name.description: A method name, a capability, or a creation id: 1 to 255 characters.

CallId.description: A call id: at most 255 characters, which the response gives back.

Invocation.description: A method call (RFC 8620 §3.2): `[name, arguments, callId]`. A method this server does not have, or whose capability is not in `using`, answers `unknownMethod`. The server has `Core/echo`, `Mailbox/get`, `Mailbox/changes`, `Mailbox/query`, `Mailbox/set`, `Email/get`, `Email/changes`, `Email/query`, `Email/set`, `Email/import` and `Thread/get`.

Arguments.description: A method's arguments, as RFC 8620 and RFC 8621 define them for it. An argument whose name starts with `#` is a back-reference to an earlier response (RFC 8620 §3.7), and gives the argument without the `#`.

ResultReference.description: A ResultReference (RFC 8620 §3.7): the response with the call id `resultOf`, which must be named `name`, read at `path`, an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer where `*` maps the rest over an array. It expands to at most `maxReferenceItems` (5000) values, and the references of one request to at most `maxReferenceBytes` (4 MiB) of JSON; past either, or when it does not resolve, the call answers `invalidResultReference`.

Response.description: A Response (RFC 8620 §3.4). It grows to at most `maxSizeResponse` (64 MiB) of JSON: past it, the request is a `limit` problem.

createdIds.description: Only when the request gave `createdIds`: those, and every creation id the request created.

ResponseInvocation.description: One call's response, with its call id: the method's response, or an `error`.

MethodResponse.description: `[name, arguments, callId]`: the method's own response arguments.

ErrorResponse.description: `["error", MethodError, callId]` (RFC 8620 §3.6.2): the call failed, the rest of the request went on.

MethodError.description: A method-level error (RFC 8620 §3.6.2, RFC 8621), inside a 200. `serverFail` is the server's or the store's failure, which `onError` is told of.

Problem.description: An RFC 7807 problem details object. The JMAP request-level errors (RFC 8620 §3.6.1) have their `urn:ietf:params:jmap:error:` type; an authentication refusal or a 404 is `about:blank`. Client text repeated in `detail` is cut after 100 characters.

limit.description: For `urn:ietf:params:jmap:error:limit`: the limit broken, by its name in the session or in the `limits` option.
